bench: Zero engine errors; 2 worlds; campaign-1 failure artifacts fetched under their own principal (3/3 hash ok); load maps published as an observation artifact; 10 organ-set artifacts with a reconstructed maturity block; 10/10 imports hash ok; 50 records; 50 reachability rows. Load maps for 135 genomes took 1.4 s. Bench notes: (1) the fixed manifest recipe (seeded on the genome only) removed C2-SFE-04's per-seed rebuild confound; (2) import share was 1.0 for every substituted set although only 100 of 200 organisms were substituted: the substituted half took over the population in every seed -- the origin-share telemetry now says takeover is the rule for any evolved material at this budget, not a property of half-credit solvers (L2-037); (3) functional_organs_used as an INTERVENTION counter made 'the functional definition produced organs' a typed condition rather than a note.
disposition_note: Assay capable (4/10 baseline, every arm reaches); the functional definition produced organs (fallback 0.0); function-defined organ chimeras do not beat length-defined chimeras by the margin (+0.097 vs 0.10, 5/10 paired wins, 4/10 vs 4/10 footholds) and their shuffled versions do as well or better (7/10): the SFE-08 negative stands under a behaviour-based organ definition.
landscape: Failed W1_d1 genotypes (SFE-01's floor organisms) are ~89% dead weight by knockout: only 11-12% of their instructions change any output on their own cell's probe episodes, and the load-bearing instructions come in runs of 2-3. Composing two such runs from different lineages gives an organism whose transfer to W2_K2 is indistinguishable from random generation 0 and from its own permutation. W2_K2 4-bit N200 G60 E16 baseline this run: 4/10 (first solved 13-49), pooled with the campaign 11/27.
science: Assay capable (random 4/10 footholds; every arm reached at least 4/10). Functional organs existed: single-instruction knockout on 135 failed W1_d1 genotypes (probe episodes of their own cell, output sequence compared) found 11-12% of instructions load-bearing and 31 organs of mean length 2.3 across the three lineages, enough that no chimera fell back to a length organ (fallback share 0.0; functional_organs_used = 100 per seed, so the intervention was applied). PRIMARY: chimera_functional - chimera_length = +0.097 held-out (paired wins 5/10; footholds 4/10 vs 4/10) against the preregistered 0.10; the machine candidate CAPABLE_NEGATIVE is accepted, and the kill arm makes the reading unambiguous: shuffled_functional (the same organs with instruction order permuted) reached 7/10 at 0.44, ABOVE the intact functional chimeras (0.35), so whatever the functional organs carry does not depend on their instruction order -- the same result C2-SFE-04 found for whole failed genotypes. Every set sits at or near the random control (random 0.36, 4/10; whole ancestors 0.32, 5/10; functional 0.35, 4/10; length 0.26, 4/10) and direct reuse is at the floor for all of them (best member 0.07-0.09 before evolution). Function-bearing organs, defined by behaviour on the source cell, transfer to W2_K2 no better than length-defined windows, shuffled versions of themselves, whole ancestors or nothing. Combined with C2-SFE-03 (components), C2-SFE-04 (whole failed genotypes) and SFE-08 (length organs), the campaign's answer to 'what do failed populations transport' is: nothing that survives a permutation or a length-matched control. Must NOT be claimed: that no organ definition can transfer (one knockout definition, one source cell, one target); that shuffled organs are better (7/10 vs 4/10 at n=10 is within noise of the random arm's 4/10).
